item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 271725
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM EDT Sun Sep 27 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Fay, located well to the west-southwest of the Azores.

Central Subtropical Atlantic (AL91):
A surface trough of low pressure located several hundred miles east
of Bermuda continues to produce an area of disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Recent satellite-derived wind data indicates the
system is producing winds of 30-35 mph and has a sharp wind shift,
though lacks a closed circulation due to its fast forward motion.
Environmental conditions appear somewhat favorable for additional
development of this system, especially as its forward motion slows
down. A tropical depression could form by the early to mid portion
of this week as the system initially moves northward before turning
eastward tomorrow over the central Subtropical Atlantic.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 272037
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fay Advisory Number  31
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...FAY BARELY A TROPICAL CYCLONE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM GMT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...28.9N 44.0W
ABOUT 1160 MI...1870 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...S OR 180 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1011 MB...29.86 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM GMT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was 
located near latitude 28.9 North, longitude 44.0 West. The 
depression is moving toward the south near 5 mph (7 km/h). A 
south-southwest to southwest motion is expected over the next couple 
of days, followed by a turn toward the west-southwest with an 
increase in forward speed by mid-week.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Fay will likely become a remnant low in a day or two, and 
dissipate later in the week.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1011 mb (29.86 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 31
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026 
440 
WTNT41 KNHC 272038
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  31
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026
 
Fay is barely a tropical cyclone. The system basically consists of a
swirl of low-level clouds with a patch of sheared and disorganized
convection located more than 60 n mi south-southwest of the center.
The initial wind speed is held at 30 kt, in general agreement with
the latest satellite intensity estimates.
 
Moderate wind shear and stable air should cause convection to pulse,
but it will likely have a hard time organizing and persisting near
the center over the next few days. Based on the expected
environmental conditions and current structure, the system is now
forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone by 36 hours, but that
transition could occur much sooner if organized deep convection
does not return. Regardless of this system's status, little change
in strength is expected during the next few days until it
dissipates later this week.
 
Fay has been moving slowly southward over the past several hours,
and a slow southward to southwestward motion in the low-level flow
is expected over the next few days. The global models show the
system degenerating into a trough in 3 to 4 days, and that is
reflected in this forecast.
